---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Fedora Server 45"
---

This guide installs the latest [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) on a clean Fedora Server 45 host.
It uses Fedora's Apache, PHP 8.5 with PHP-FPM, MariaDB 11.8, Valkey, and Supervisor packages. [Fedora Server downloads](https://fedoraproject.org/server/download/)

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch.
Evaluate it on an isolated host before deployment.
Use this procedure for a new database. For an existing instance, see [Plan a 2.5 upgrade](#fedora-install-upgrade).
:::

The package and application checks ran in a Fedora 45 x86_64 container with services started directly.
Verify systemd startup and SELinux enforcement on your Fedora Server host.

## Prepare the host {#fedora-install-prepare}

Use an administrative account with `sudo`, a DNS name, and a trusted TLS certificate and key for that name.
Keep web access restricted to administrators until you change the bootstrap password.
Size the host and database storage for the expected load. [Instance requirements](../requirements/index.qmd)

Use Fedora's packaged MariaDB 11.8 series for this procedure.
MISP uses Valkey through the PHP Redis extension and Redis settings. [MariaDB 11.8 packages](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/mariadb11.8/mariadb11.8-server/) · [Valkey package](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/valkey/valkey/)

```bash
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh
sudo dnf install ca-certificates composer curl file-libs gcc git gnupg2 httpd iproute \
  mariadb11.8 mariadb11.8-server mod_ssl openssl php-bcmath php-cli php-fpm php-gd \
  php-intl php-mbstring php-mysqlnd php-pecl-apcu php-pecl-redis6 php-pecl-zip \
  php-process php-xml policycoreutils-python-utils procps-ng python3-devel \
  python3-pip ssdeep-devel supervisor unzip valkey
php --version
php --ri redis
php --ri pdo_mysql
mariadb --version
```

Set `memory_limit = 2048M` in `/etc/php.d/99-misp.ini` for the initial definitions import and PHP runtime.
Check the setting with `php -r 'echo ini_get("memory_limit"), PHP_EOL;'`.

## Install MISP and its dependencies {#fedora-install-source}

Keep the checkout on the `3.0_wip` branch and use its matching submodules.
Run Git, Composer, Python dependency installation, and Cake commands as `apache`.

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0750 /var/www/MISP /var/lib/misp \
  /var/lib/misp/composer /var/lib/misp/attachments
sudo -u apache git clone --branch 3.0_wip --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/MISP/MISP.git /var/www/MISP
sudo -u apache git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch

sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist
sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app check-platform-reqs --no-dev
sudo -u apache python3 -m venv /var/www/MISP/venv
sudo -u apache env HOME=/var/lib/misp /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip install \
  -r /var/www/MISP/requirements.txt
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip check
```

## Initialize MariaDB, Valkey, and MISP {#fedora-install-database}

Create `/etc/my.cnf.d/90-misp.cnf`, owned by root with mode `0644`, to restrict MariaDB to loopback.
In `/etc/valkey/valkey.conf`, keep `bind 127.0.0.1 -::1` and `protected-mode yes`.

```ini
[mariadb]
bind-address=127.0.0.1
```

Start both services and check for `PONG` from Valkey.
Open an administrative MariaDB session over its Unix socket with history disabled.

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now mariadb valkey
valkey-cli ping
sudo env MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null mariadb --protocol=SOCKET
```

Create the database and the application account for the loopback TCP connection.
Use a unique password and retain it for the MISP database settings.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE misp
    CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci;
CREATE USER 'misp'@'127.0.0.1' IDENTIFIED BY 'REPLACE_WITH_DATABASE_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON misp.* TO 'misp'@'127.0.0.1';
EXIT;
```

Load the branch's MariaDB schema and copy the configuration templates.

```bash
sudo mariadb --protocol=SOCKET misp < /var/www/MISP/INSTALL/MARIADB.sql
for name in bootstrap config core database; do
  sudo install -o apache -g apache -m 0640 \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.default.php" "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.php"
done
```

In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/database.php`, set `host` to `127.0.0.1`, `login` to `misp`, and `password` to the database password.
Keep `database` set to `misp`.
In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/config.php`, set the following `MISP` keys using your hostname and organization.

```php
'baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'external_baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'org' => 'Your organization',
'osuser' => 'apache',
'python_bin' => '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python',
'attachments_dir' => '/var/lib/misp/attachments',
'redis_host' => '127.0.0.1',
'background_jobs' => false,
```

Set `Security.salt` to a unique value from `openssl rand -hex 32` in the same file.
Keep jobs disabled while applying schema updates, creating the administrator, and importing the bundled definitions.

```bash
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates
sudo sh -c 'umask 077
  runuser -u apache -- /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake User init > /root/misp-bootstrap-api-key'
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin updateJSON
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
```

Keep the bootstrap API key private.
Confirm that schema diagnostics report `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.

### Set up the instance signing key {#fedora-install-gnupg}

Create the signing key in a private Bash session and substitute your instance's email address.

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0700 /var/lib/misp/gnupg
read -r -s -p 'Instance GnuPG passphrase: ' gpg_passphrase
printf '\n'
printf '%s\n' "$gpg_passphrase" | sudo -u apache gpg --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg \
  --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 \
  --quick-generate-key misp@example.org ed25519 sign never
unset gpg_passphrase
sudo -u apache sh -c 'gpg --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --armor --export \
  misp@example.org > /var/www/MISP/app/webroot/gpg.asc'
```

Set `GnuPG.homedir`, `GnuPG.email`, and `GnuPG.password` in `app/Config/config.php` to the directory, email address, and passphrase you used.
Include the key and configuration in your protected backups. [Instance and user keys](../cryptographic-keys/index.qmd)

## Configure SELinux and HTTPS {#fedora-install-web}

Keep SELinux enforcing and set persistent labels for data that PHP must write.
Use your network policy to limit outbound connections. The SELinux network boolean permits Apache and PHP-FPM to reach local services and make outbound connections for MISP. [Fedora SELinux documentation](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/quick-docs/selinux-getting-started/)

```bash
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/www/MISP/app/(Config|tmp)(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/www/MISP/app/files/scripts/tmp(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t '/var/lib/misp'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/lib/misp/(attachments|gnupg)(/.*)?'
sudo restorecon -R /var/www/MISP /var/lib/misp
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect on
```

In `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf`, replace the packaged example `<VirtualHost>` block with the following.
Keep the global SSL settings and `Listen 443 https`.
Use your actual hostname, certificate chain, and private key paths.

```apache
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    Redirect permanent / https://misp.example.org/
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/MISP/app/webroot
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key

    <Directory /var/www/MISP/app/webroot>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride FileInfo
        Require all granted
        DirectoryIndex index.php
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

Fedora's `/etc/httpd/conf.d/php.conf` passes PHP requests to the packaged FPM pool on `/run/php-fpm/www.sock`.
Check that `rewrite`, `headers`, and `proxy_fcgi` appear in `sudo httpd -M`.
Use `AllowOverride FileInfo` to enable the repository's rewrite and API authorization rules.

```bash
sudo restorecon -v /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key
sudo php-fpm -t
sudo httpd -t
sudo systemctl enable --now php-fpm httpd
```

If firewalld is active, allow `https` in the zone serving your administration network.
Allow `http` there if clients will use the redirect. [Fedora firewalld documentation](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/quick-docs/firewalld/)
Verify the TLS certificate and sign in as `admin@admin.test` with password `admin`.
Change the password before granting other clients access. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

## Start and verify the background workers {#fedora-install-workers}

Add the authenticated TCP endpoint below to `/etc/supervisord.conf` and keep it on loopback.
Keep the packaged Unix socket for local `supervisorctl` commands.
Choose a separate password for the MISP worker-management API.

```ini
[inet_http_server]
port=127.0.0.1:9001
username=supervisor
password=REPLACE_WITH_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD
```

Create `/etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini` with five queue workers and one dedicated scheduler.

```bash
{
  printf '%s\n' '[group:misp-workers]' \
    'programs=default,email,cache,prio,update,scheduler'
  for worker in default email cache prio update scheduler; do
    if [ "$worker" = scheduler ]; then
      cake_command=scheduler_worker
    else
      cake_command="start_worker $worker"
    fi
    cat <<EOF

[program:$worker]
command=/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake $cake_command
directory=/var/www/MISP
user=apache
autostart=true
autorestart=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/MISP/app/tmp/logs/$worker-worker.log
EOF
  done
} | sudo tee /etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini > /dev/null
```

In the `SimpleBackgroundJobs` section of `app/Config/config.php`, set `redis_host` and `supervisor_host` to `127.0.0.1`.
Keep `supervisor_port` at `9001` and set `supervisor_user` and `supervisor_password` to match the Supervisor configuration.
Set `MISP.background_jobs` to `true`.

```bash
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/supervisord.conf
sudo systemctl enable --now supervisord
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin getWorkers
sudo systemctl status mariadb valkey php-fpm httpd supervisord --no-pager
sudo ss -lnt
```

Check that all six worker processes report `RUNNING` and that MariaDB, Valkey, and Supervisor listen only on loopback.
Save and search for an unpublished, organization-only test event.
Verify that a queued job completes before enabling synchronization or scheduled feeds. [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)
Before enabling protected synchronization, verify that the **GnuPG** check reports **OK** under **Administration → Server Settings & Maintenance → Services** with SELinux enforcing. [System health checks](../administration/index.qmd#server-settings-and-maintenance)

## Plan a 2.5 upgrade {#fedora-install-upgrade}

For an existing MISP 2.5 database, use the [offline upgrade procedure](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd) to back up the instance, rehearse on a restored copy, and run `Admin runUpgrade` on the latest `3.0_wip` checkout.
Use the `apache` account for MISP commands and restart PHP-FPM with `sudo systemctl restart php-fpm` after the migration.
Time the conversion on a representative copy to estimate your maintenance window.
